title: 6 Things You Must Do On The First Day Of School
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin lays out six essentials for a first day of school that sets the tone for the entire year: making a genuine connection with students, modeling one routine (like entering the classroom) with excellence to establish a standard, having fun so students associate the classroom with enjoyment, promising to protect their right to learn, following through by teaching the classroom management plan as a safeguard rather than a threat, and diving into real academic content so students see the room as a place of serious learning. He frames the first day as reflecting the teacher's 'vision of a dream class,' not a scripted checklist. The article closes by reassuring teachers that pursuing these six items doesn't require perfection—natural imperfection and authenticity, delivered with warmth, will still win students over.
points: Build rapport immediately by greeting students warmly and signaling they're now part of a unique classroom community.
Model one key routine (such as morning entry) with excellent, step-by-step precision to set a template for how all future routines will be taught.
Incorporate genuine fun on day one—it fuels motivation, attentiveness, and gives the teacher leverage to expect hard work and respect.
Promise to protect students' right to learn and enjoy school, then follow through by teaching the classroom management plan as a safeguard, not a punishment system.
Dive into a real, high-interest academic lesson on day one to establish the classroom as a serious place of learning from the very start.
quotes: You have one opportunity to start your school year on the right classroom management foot, one shot to propel your first day of school into the best learning experience your students have ever had.
Your initial friendliness and open, welcoming heart will put them at ease and spark an immediate desire to please you, follow your lead, and pay forward your kindness throughout the classroom.
This first routine, when taught with depth and precision, and then practiced successfully, paves the way for all other routines to be learned quickly and thereafter performed with excellence.
You’re going to promise them that you will protect their special community, that you will protect their right to learn and enjoy school.
Establish from the get-go that your classroom is in the business of learning by diving into a challenging academic lesson (or two or three) on the first day of school.
Have your content, your objectives, and the overall tone of the day pictured clearly in your mind, but allow yourself room to mess up, to stumble over your words.
